rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Beyond their common trade subject, the two proclamations use a highly parallel sequence of recitals: a finding that existing duties unduly burden foreign trade; publication of article lists and review by the tariff commission; public hearings through a committee designated by the Special Representative; receipt of advice from the same cabinet departments; execution of a bilateral trade agreement through a duly empowered representative; and implementation through annex-based modification of the Tariff Schedules. Their operative provisions likewise culminate in annex-based TSUS modification with a specified effective date. C08 and C23 share much of this machinery and language, but C03 is the closest overall match because it combines the full recital sequence with nearly the same two-part operative structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: certain existing duties of the United States are unduly burdening and restricting the foreign trade of the United States and ... one or more of the purposes of the Trade Act would be promoted by entering into the trade agreement with India
shared_material.parent_excerpt: certain existing duties or other import restrictions ... were unduly burdening and restricting the foreign trade of the United States and ... one or more of the purposes ... would be promoted by entering into the trade agreement with Japan
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel presidential finding supporting entry into the identified bilateral trade agreement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: published and furnished the United States International Trade Commission ... with lists of articles which may be considered for modifications or continuance ... The USITC, after holding public hearings, has advised the President ... as to the probable economic effect
shared_material.parent_excerpt: published and furnished to the Tariff Commission lists of articles which may be considered for modification or continuance ... and the Tariff Commission, after holding public hearings, has advised the President ... as to the probable economic effect
shared_material.explanation: Substantially identical procedural recital, updated for the later statute and commission name.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations designated the Trade Policy Staff Committee to afford an opportunity, through public hearings and other means, for any interested person to present his views
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations ... designated the Trade Information Committee to afford an opportunity, through public hearings and other means, for any interested person to present his views
shared_material.explanation: Concrete administrative machinery and phrasing are reused, with the committee name changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President has received information and advice ... from the Departments of Agriculture, Commerce, Defense, Interior, Labor, State and the Treasury
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the President has received information and advice ... from the Departments of Agriculture, Commerce, Defense, Interior, Labor, State, and the Treasury
shared_material.explanation: The same ordered interagency-advice recital appears in both documents.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President, through his duly empowered representative ... entered into a temporary trade agreement with India
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I, through my duly empowered representative, have entered into a trade agreement with Japan
shared_material.explanation: Closely parallel formulation identifies execution of the bilateral agreement as the predicate for proclamation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Part 2 of the Appendix to the TSUS is modified as provided in Annexes I and II to this proclamation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Tariff Schedules of the United States shall be modified ... as provided for in Appendix A to this proclamation
shared_material.explanation: Both implement the agreement through annex- or appendix-specified tariff-schedule modifications, completing the same drafting sequence.
